text vs p.10 Table 2 / p.7 Conclusions | conclusion overstates the data | "Composites of LaRC-SI/regolith and polyethylene/regolith are shown to have good structural properties as well as being effective shields from GCR radiation" vs Table 2 "Specimen 101 580 / Specimen 102 633" vs "No Shield 474" | In the only neutron SEU test, both LaRC-SI/regolith specimens gave more upsets than no shield (the text says "within statistical error"). PE/regolith composites were never radiation-tested in this report, and GCR shielding of the composites was only calculated (Fig. 1), with Martian regolith.

text vs p.14 Fig. 5(b) | text not supported by figure | "The Young's modulus of neutron-exposed specimens for both regolith 101 and 102 were decreased by 10% from the baseline" vs Fig. 5(b) | Digitized points: 101 baseline about 5.66–6.13 GPa vs neutron about 5.02–5.44 GPa (about -11%, consistent), but 102 baseline about 7.52–8.62 GPa vs neutron about 6.80–8.70 GPa (mean about -3%). text vs p.14 Fig. 5(b) | text not supported by figure | "the proton-exposed specimens for both regolith 101 and 102 composites experienced an increase in the Young's modulus" vs Fig. 5(b) | For 101, the proton-exposed points (about 4.98, 5.67, 7.10 GPa) are spread around the baseline (about 5.66–6.13 GPa) rather than clearly higher.
